answer: Give every new identity a hollow reputation shell recorded on an ivory ledger. It fills only through live velvet check-ins: unannounced, interactive tasks at random times that cannot be scripted in advance or run in parallel. A missed check-in empties the shell and doubles the sessions needed to refill it, so the tenth clone of one operator needs far more than ten times the attention — a cost in irreplaceable supervised time that no number of clones can share.
